comments.body:
I reviewed the full solution to rm-11206 (semi-supervised learning of Boolean disjunctions with a compatibility/pair structure), verified its correctness, and closed a residual interpretive gap.

**Established result.** Answer: YES. Algorithm 1 (Valiant-style literal elimination on the first components of the labeled pairs) runs in poly(n,1/eps,1/delta) time, uses m = O((n ln(1/eps)+ln(1/delta))/eps) labeled examples and no unlabeled pairs, and outputs a disjunction with err_D <= eps w.p. >= 1-delta. This count is poly(m*); in fact m = O(m* · ln(1/eps)).

**Checks performed.**
- Lemma (consistency of literal-elimination): correct; confirmed numerically on 2000 random realizable disjunction samples (no inconsistency).
- Lemma (VCdim(C) in [n, n+1]): correct (basis-point shattering; halfspace embedding).
- Reduction lemma (pair-error = one-sided error on x_1-marginal; kept sample iid, realizable by h*): correct.
- Main correctness theorem: correct application of the BEHW/Anthony-Bartlett consistent-learner PAC bound with d = n+1. End-to-end empirically validated: n=8, eps=delta=0.1, m=3894 gives empirical failure rate 0.0 over 300 trials.
- Proposition on m*: worst-case-over-D baseline = Theta((n+ln(1/delta))/eps) up to a ln(1/eps) factor; upper bound via C(U) ⊆ C, lower bound via the diagonal distribution D = law of (x,x) where C(U)=C a.s. Correct.

**Gap closed.** The delicate point is the meaning of m*(eps,delta,n), which the notation makes depend only on eps,delta,n (no D). I added Remark (Robustness of the comparison to the interpretation of m*) right after Proposition 1's proof. It shows the YES answer is not an artifact of the worst-case reading: under the per-D reading, m* loses its n-dependence when C(U) collapses, but then NO algorithm could be poly(m*) uniformly over all compatible D (any correct learner needs Omega(n/eps) labels on the diagonal distribution where C(U)=C). So the per-D reading makes the question vacuously negative for every algorithm and cannot be intended; under the only meaningful (worst-case-over-D) reading, the answer is affirmative.

The proof is now complete and rigorous. (No LaTeX toolchain in workspace; begin/end document and ref labels checked for balance manually.)
